english.heading: Food Forest Design
body: Build a living food system in layers.
Grow food from tall canopy down to root crops.
Use vertical space, soil life, shade, and moisture together.
Learn how to design and establish a food forest for your farm.

heading.text: Nkunguhato wa Food Forest
heading.backTranslation: Design of a Food Forest

body.text: Aka sisiteme ya swakudya leyi hanyaka hi swiyenge swo hambana.
body.backTranslation: Build a food system that lives in different layers.

body.text: Byala swakudya ku suka eka canopy ya mirhi yo leha ku fika eka root crops.
body.backTranslation: Plant food from the canopy of tall trees down to root crops.

body.text: Tirhisa ndhawu ya le henhla ni le hansi, leswi hanyaka emisaveni, ndzhuti (shade) ni mati swin'we.
body.backTranslation: Use the upper and lower space, things that live in the soil, shade and water together.

body.text: Dyondza ku hlela ni ku sungula food forest epurasini ra wena.
body.backTranslation: Learn to plan and start a food forest on your farm.

english.heading: Why This Matters
body: A food forest grows useful plants at different heights.
Good design can combine harvests, shade and soil cover. Plants still compete for light, water and nutrients.
Plan the care you can provide and watch how the planting changes.

heading.text: Ha yini leswi swi ri swa nkoka
heading.backTranslation: Why this is important

body.text: Food forest yi kurisa swimila leswi pfunaka leswi nga ni ku leha ko hambana.
body.backTranslation: A food forest grows helpful plants that have different heights/lengths.

body.text: Nkunguhato lowunene wu nga hlanganisa ntshovelo, ndzhuti (shade) ni ku funengeta misava. Swimila swa ha phikizana hi ku vonakala ka dyambu, mati ni nutrients.
body.backTranslation: A good plan can combine harvest, shade and ground cover. Plants still compete for sunlight, water and nutrients.

body.text: Hlela nhlayiso lowu u nga kotaka ku wu endla, kutani u languta ndlela leyi swimila swi cincaka ha yona.
body.backTranslation: Plan maintenance that you are able to do, then watch how the plants change.

english.heading: Learning Outcomes
body: Name the seven commonly described food-forest layers.
Check plants against your site, local ecology and the approved project list.
Plan establishment and ongoing care without assuming a fixed date for harvest or canopy closure.

heading.text: Leswi u nga ta kota ku swi endla
heading.backTranslation: What you will be able to do

body.text: Boxa swiyenge swa 7 leswi tolovelekeke ku hlamusela food forest.
body.backTranslation: Box the 7 layers that are commonly used to describe a food forest.

body.text: Kambela swimila hi ku ya hi ndhawu ya wena, ecology ya ndhawu ni approved project list.
body.backTranslation: Check plants according to your place, the ecology of the place and the approved project list.

body.text: Hlela establishment ni nhlayiso lowu yaka emahlweni, u nga teki leswaku ku ta va ni siku leri vekiweke ra ntshovelo kumbe ra ku pfaleka ka canopy.
body.backTranslation: Plan establishment and ongoing maintenance; do not assume there will be a set date for harvest or canopy closing.

english.heading: The Forest Uses Every Layer
body: An indigenous forest fills the space from the highest branches to the roots.
Different plants use the light and moisture available at their level.
A food forest copies this pattern with productive species.
The result is not one crop in one row, but many useful layers growing together.

heading.text: Nhova (forest) yi tirhisa swiyenge hinkwato
heading.backTranslation: A forest uses all the layers

body.text: Nhova ya indigenous (forest) yi tata ndhawu ku sukela eka marhavi ya le henhla swinene ku fika eka timitsu.
body.backTranslation: An indigenous forest fills the space from the very high branches down to the roots.

body.text: Swimila swo hambana swi tirhisa ku vonakala ka dyambu ni mati lama kumekaka eka xiyenge xa swona.
body.backTranslation: Different plants use the sunlight and water that is available in their layer.

body.text: Food forest yi tekelela xivumbeko lexi hi mixaka ya swimila leswi humesaka vuyelo.
body.backTranslation: A food forest imitates the shape/structure that is made of kinds of plants that produce yield/fruit.

body.text: Vuyelo a hi xibyariwa xin'we eka layini yin'we, kambe i swiyenge swo tala leswi pfunaka leswi kulaka swin'we.
body.backTranslation: The yield is not one crop in one row, but many layers that help those that grow together.

english.heading: Watch: Read the Seven Planting Layers
body: Find seven planting layers.
Tall trees form the canopy.
Smaller trees grow below it.
Then look for woody shrubs.
Herbaceous plants have soft stems.
Ground cover spreads across the surface.
Root crops grow below the surface.
Climbers use suitable supports.
These are planning layers, not fixed height bands. Choose plants and spacing for your site.

heading.text: Languta: Hlaya Swiyenge swa 7 swa Ku Byala
heading.backTranslation: Look: Read the 7 Layers of Planting

body.text: Kuma swiyenge swa 7 swa ku byala.
body.backTranslation: Find the 7 layers of planting.

body.text: Mirhi yo leha yi vumba canopy.
body.backTranslation: Tall trees form the canopy.

body.text: Mirhi leyitsongo yi kula ehansi ka canopy.
body.backTranslation: Small trees grow below the canopy.

body.text: Endzhaku ka sweswo, lava swihlahla leswi nga ni swiphunga swo tiya (woody).
body.backTranslation: After that, look for shrubs that have strong stems (woody).

body.text: Swimila swa herbaceous swi ni swiphunga swo olova.
body.backTranslation: Herbaceous plants have soft stems.

body.text: Swimila leswi funengetaka misava swi hangalaka ehenhla ka misava.
body.backTranslation: Ground-covering plants spread over the top of the soil.

body.text: Root crops swi kula ehansi ka misava.
body.backTranslation: Root crops grow under the soil.

body.text: Swimila swo khandziya swi tirhisa swilo leswi faneleke leswi swi nga khandziyaka ehenhla ka swona.
body.backTranslation: Climbing plants use suitable things that they can climb up on.

body.text: Leswi i swiyenge swa ku hlela, a hi swiyenge leswi nga ni ku leha loku nga cinciki. Hlawula swimila ni mpfhuka exikarhi ka swimila hi ku ya hi ndhawu ya wena.
body.backTranslation: These are not planting/layout sections, they are not sections that have a fixed length that does not change. Choose plants and the space between plants according to your place.

english.heading: The Seven Layers
body: Think of tall canopy, smaller trees, shrubs and herbaceous plants.
Ground cover protects the surface, root crops grow below it, and climbers use suitable supports.
The heights and spacing depend on the plants and site. These are planning layers, not fixed height bands.

heading.text: Swiyenge swa 7
heading.backTranslation: 7 layers

body.text: Anakanyisa hi canopy yo leha, mirhi leyitsongo, swihlahla ni swimila swa herbaceous.
body.backTranslation: Think about a tall canopy, small trees, shrubs and herbaceous plants.

body.text: Swimila leswi funengetaka misava swi sirhelela ehenhla ka misava, swibyariwa swa timitsu (root crops) swi kula ehansi ka yona, naswona swimila swo khandziya swi tirhisa swilo leswi faneleke leswi swi nga khandziyaka ehenhla ka swona.
body.backTranslation: Ground-covering plants protect the top of the soil, root crops grow beneath it, and climbing plants use suitable things that they can climb up on top of them.

body.text: Ku leha ka swimila ni ndhawu leyi nga exikarhi ka swona swi titshege hi swimila ni ndhawu. Leswi i swiyenge swa ku hlela, a hi swiyenge leswi nga ni ku leha loku nga cinciki.
body.backTranslation: The height of the plants and the space between them depend on the plants and the site. These are planning layers; they are not layers with an unchanging height.

english.heading: Read a Layered Planting Example
body: The original Highveld example includes Wild Fig or pecan above lemon, naartjie and black mulberry.
It places Cape gooseberry and Wild Medlar with vegetables, wild garlic, sweet potato and granadilla.
Treat this as a layout example, not permission to plant every species. Check identity, frost tolerance, mature size and local restrictions first.

heading.text: Hlaya Xikombiso xa Ku Byala hi Swiyenge
heading.backTranslation: Read the Example of Planting by Layers

body.text: Xikombiso xa masungulo xa le Highveld xi katsa Wild Fig kumbe pecan ehenhla ka lemon, naartjie ni black mulberry.
body.backTranslation: A starting example from the Highveld includes Wild Fig or pecan above lemon, naartjie and black mulberry.

body.text: Xi veka Cape gooseberry ni Wild Medlar swin'we ni miroho, wild garlic, sweet potato ni granadilla.
body.backTranslation: It places Cape gooseberry and Wild Medlar together with vegetables, wild garlic, sweet potato and granadilla.

body.text: Teka leswi tanihi xikombiso xa ku vekiwa ka swimila, a hi mpfumelelo wo byala mixaka hinkwayo. Rhanga u kambela leswaku swi nga xiswona, frost tolerance, vukulu bya swona loko swi kurile ni swiyimiso swa ndhawu leswi yirisaka.
body.backTranslation: Take this as an example of the placement of plants; it is not permission to plant all the kinds. First check what they are like, frost tolerance, their size when grown, and the site requirements that are suitable.

english.heading: Care Changes as Plants Grow
body: Young plants need establishment care: moisture checks, weed control and protection from damage.
As plants grow, shade and leaf litter change conditions below them.
Check competition and access. Prune, thin or adjust lower planting when observations call for it; the system does not become care-free on a fixed birthday.

heading.text: Nhlayiso yi cinca loko swimila swi kula
heading.backTranslation: Maintenance changes when the plants grow.

body.text: Swimila leswintshwa swi lava nhlayiso wa establishment (ku swi pfuna swi dzika timitsu ni ku tshama endzhaku ka ku byariwa): ku kambela ku tsakama ka misava, ku lawula swimila leswi nga laviwiki ni ku sirhelela eka ku onhiwa.
body.backTranslation: Plants that are newly planted need establishment care (to help them put down roots and stay on afterwards, after being planted): checking soil moisture, controlling unwanted plants and protecting against damage.

body.text: Loko swimila swi ri karhi swi kula, ndzhuti (shade) ni leaf litter swi cinca xiyimo xa le hansi ka swona.
body.backTranslation: While plants are growing, shade and leaf litter change the condition beneath them.

body.text: Kambela ku phikizana ni ndlela yo fikelela. Tsema marhavi ya swimila, endla thinning (ku susa swimila leswi hlawuriweke hi ku helela) kumbe lulamisa ku byala ka le hansi loko leswi vonekeke swi swi lava; sisiteme a yi hundzuki yi nga lavi nhlayiso hi siku ra ku velekiwa leri vekiweke.
body.backTranslation: Check competition and the way of access. Cut plant branches, do thinning (removing selected plants completely) or adjust the low planting when what has been seen requires it; the system does not become one that needs no care on a set day of being born/established.

english.heading: Choose for Your Site
body: Check local rainfall, frost, heat, soil and water availability before choosing plants.
Mango can suffer frost damage. Quince needs suitable winter chilling for reliable cropping.
A regional label or a sheltered corner is not enough. Confirm each plant and variety with reliable local guidance.

heading.text: Hlawula hi ku ya hi Ndhawu ya Wena
heading.backTranslation: Choose according to Your Place

body.text: Kambela mpfula ya ndhawu, xiqhwa, ku hisa, misava ni mati lama kumekaka u nga si hlawula swimila.
body.backTranslation: Check the local rain, frost, heat, soil and the water that is available before you choose plants.

body.text: Mango yi nga onhiwa hi xiqhwa. Quince yi lava winter chilling leyi faneleke leswaku yi humesa mihandzu hi ndlela leyi tshembekaka.
body.backTranslation: Mango can be damaged by frost. Quince needs suitable winter chilling so that it produces fruit reliably.

body.text: Vito ra xifundzha kumbe nkona (corner) lowu sirhelelekeke a swi ringani. Tiyisisa ximila xin'wana ni xin'wana ni muxaka wa xona hi nkongomiso wa ndhawu lowu tshembekaka.
body.backTranslation: The name of a province or a sheltered corner is not sufficient. Verify each plant and its kind with a reliable local guide/direction.

english.heading: Watch: Match the Species to the Climate
body: Climate decides which species belong.
On the Highveld, choose cold-tolerant trees and shrubs; on the KZN coast and Lowveld, choose warm-climate species.
Match every plant to your site.

heading.text: Languta: Fambisa Tinxaka ni Xiyimo xa Moya
heading.backTranslation: Look: Match Kinds and Climate

body.text: Xiyimo xa moya xi hlawula leswaku i tinxaka tihi leti fanelaka.
body.backTranslation: The condition of the air/weather determines which kinds are suitable.

body.text: Eka Highveld, hlawula mirhi ni swihlahla leswi tiyiselaka vuhola; eka KZN coast ni Lowveld, hlawula tinxaka ta ndhawu leyi hisaka.
body.backTranslation: On the Highveld, choose trees and shrubs that tolerate cold; on the KZN coast and Lowveld, choose kinds of a hot area.

body.text: Fambisanisa ximila xin'wana ni xin'wana ni ndhawu ya wena.
body.backTranslation: Match each plant to your place/site.

english.heading: Check the Highveld Examples
body: The original list includes pecan, walnut and indigenous fig; apple, pear, plum, black mulberry and loquat; rosemary, Wild Medlar, Cape gooseberry and Barbados cherry.
This list is not a blanket recommendation. Check each plant against frost, soil, mature size and the approved local species list.
Keep existing legal and project restrictions in force. Do not plant from a picture alone.

heading.text: Kambela Swikombiso swa Highveld
heading.backTranslation: Check Highveld Examples

body.text: Lisiti ya masungulo yi katsa pecan, walnut ni indigenous fig; apple, pear, plum, black mulberry ni loquat; rosemary, Wild Medlar, Cape gooseberry ni Barbados cherry.
body.backTranslation: A starting list includes pecan, walnut and indigenous fig; apple, pear, plum, black mulberry and loquat; rosemary, Wild Medlar, Cape gooseberry and Barbados cherry.

body.text: Lisiti leyi a hi xitsundzuxo lexi tirhaka eka swimila hinkwaswo. Kambela ximila xin'wana ni xin'wana hi ku ringanisa ni xiqhwa, misava, vukulu bya xona loko xi kurile ni approved local species list.
body.backTranslation: This list is not a reminder/instruction that works for all plants. Check each plant by matching it with frost, soil, its size when grown and the approved local species list.

body.text: Hlayisa swiyimiso swa nawu ni swa phurojeke leswi yirisaka leswi nga kona swi ri karhi swi tirha. U nga byali hi xifaniso ntsena.
body.backTranslation: Keep the legal and project rules that restrict, which are in force while working. Do not plant by picture only.

english.heading: Check the Warm-Region Examples
body: The original warm-region examples include mango, avocado, Natal Mahogany, banana, pawpaw, litchi, Wild Fig, Barbados cherry and Wild Dagga.
Marula, Mopane and baobab also appear in the Limpopo examples. Local suitability still needs checking.
Useful trees are not automatically edible. Confirm identity and safe use; a landscape photograph is not a food-identification guide.

heading.text: Kambela Swikombiso swa Ndhawu leyi Hisaka
heading.backTranslation: Check Examples of a Hot Area

body.text: Swikombiso swa masungulo swa swifundzha leswi hisaka swi katsa mango, avocado, Natal Mahogany, banana, pawpaw, litchi, Wild Fig, Barbados cherry ni Wild Dagga.
body.backTranslation: Starting examples of hot provinces include mango, avocado, Natal Mahogany, banana, pawpaw, litchi, Wild Fig, Barbados cherry and Wild Dagga.

body.text: Marula, Mopane ni baobab swi tlhela swi kumeka eka swikombiso swa Limpopo. Ku fanela ka ndhawu ku ha lava ku kambisisiwa.
body.backTranslation: Marula, Mopane and baobab are also found in the Limpopo examples. Site suitability still needs to be checked.

body.text: Ku pfuna ka mirhi ntsena a swi vuli leswaku yi nga dyiwa. Tiyisekisa leswaku i mirhi yihi ni leswaku yi tirhisiwa hi ndlela leyi nga riki ni khombo; xifaniso lexi tekiweke xa ndhawu a hi nkongomiso wo tiva swakudya.
body.backTranslation: The usefulness of trees alone does not say they can be eaten. Make sure which trees they are and that they are used in a way that has no danger; a picture taken of a place is not a guide to knowing foods.

english.heading: Include Locally Appropriate Indigenous Plants
body: Locally appropriate indigenous plants can support habitat as part of the design.
Choose for your ecosystem and the useful role of each plant. There is no sourced percentage target in this lesson.
Protect existing natural vegetation. Do not turn healthy grassland into a food forest simply because trees are useful elsewhere.

heading.text: Katsa swimila swa indigenous leswi faneleke laha
heading.backTranslation: Include suitable indigenous plants here.

body.text: Swimila swa indigenous leswi faneleke ndhawu swi nga seketela habitat tanihi xiphemu xa nkunguhato.
body.backTranslation: Indigenous plants that suit the place can support habitat as part of the design/plan.

body.text: Hlawula hi ku ya hi ecosystem ya wena ni ntirho lowu pfunaka wa ximila xin'wana ni xin'wana. A ku na xikongomelo xa phesenti lexi nga ni xihlovo eka dyondzo leyi.
body.backTranslation: Choose according to your ecosystem and the helpful function of each plant. There is no percentage target that has a source in this course.

body.text: Sirhelela swimila swa ntumbuluko leswi nga kona. U nga hundzuluxi ndhawu ya byanyi leyi hanyeke kahle ku va food forest ntsena hikuva mirhi yi pfuna kun'wana.
body.backTranslation: Protect the natural plants that are there. Do not turn a healthy grassland/grass area into a food forest only because trees help in other ways.

english.heading: Plan the Sequence for the Site
body: Start by checking the site, water supply and care available. Protect exposed soil early.
Temporary support plants may provide shelter and useful cut material where appropriate.
Main trees and lower layers can be introduced as conditions allow. Ground cover need not wait until the end; avoid plants competing with young trees.

heading.text: Hlela Ku Landzelelana ka Ndhawu
heading.backTranslation: Plan the Sequence of the Place

body.text: Sungula hi ku kambela ndhawu, mati lama kumekaka ni nhlayiso lowu kumekaka. Sirhelela misava leyi nga funengetiwangiki eku sunguleni.
body.backTranslation: Start by checking the site, available water and available care. Protect soil that is not covered at the start.

body.text: Support plants swa nkarhinyana swi nga nyika xisirhelelo ni swilo leswi tsemiweke leswi pfunaka laha swi faneleke.
body.backTranslation: Temporary support plants can give protection and cuttings that help where suitable.

body.text: Mirhi ya nkoka ni swiyenge swa le hansi swi nga nghenisiwa loko swiyimo swi pfumelela. Swimila leswi funengetaka misava a swi lavi ku rindza ku fika emakumu; papalata swimila leswi phikizanaka ni mirhi leyintshwa.
body.backTranslation: Important trees and lower layers can be brought in when conditions allow. Ground-covering plants do not need to wait until the end; avoid plants that compete with new trees.

english.heading: Watch: Care for a Young Food Forest
body: This picture shows a young food forest. Start with an area you can care for.
Protect exposed soil early. Here, loose mulch covers the soil.
Keep mulch away from the trunk. Notice the clear space at the tree's base.
Watch for competition. The farmer is removing grass near the young tree.
Before adding more plants, check moisture, shelter and the care you can provide. Let what you observe guide your next step.

heading.text: Languta: Hlayisa Food Forest leyitsongo
heading.backTranslation: Look: Maintain a small Food Forest

body.text: Xifaniso lexi xi komba food forest leyitsongo. Sungula hi ndhawu leyi u nga yi hlayisaka.
body.backTranslation: This picture shows a small food forest. Start with a place that you can maintain.

body.text: Sirhelela misava leyi nga funengetiwangiki eku sunguleni. Laha, mulch wo olova wu funengeta misava.
body.backTranslation: Protect soil that is not covered at the start. Here, light mulch covers the soil.

body.text: Hlayisa mulch kule ni nsinya wa murhi (trunk). Xiya ndhawu leyi pfulekeke ehansi swinene ka nsinya wa murhi.
body.backTranslation: Keep mulch away from the trunk. Notice the open area right at the base of the tree trunk.

body.text: Tivonele ku phikizana. Mulimi u susa byanyi ekusuhi ni murhi lowutsongo.
body.backTranslation: Watch for competition. The farmer removes grass/weeds near the small tree.

body.text: U nga si engetela swimila swin'wana, kambela ku tsakama ka misava, xisirhelelo ni nhlayiso lowu u nga wu endlaka. Tshika leswi u swi xiyaka swi kongomisa goza leri landzelaka.
body.backTranslation: Before adding other plants, check soil moisture, protection and the care that you have given. Leave what you notice to guide the next round/season.

english.heading: Prepare a Manageable First Area
body: Begin with an area you can water and maintain. Check existing vegetation before clearing.
Where appropriate, plain cardboard under suitable mulch can suppress unwanted growth. Keep water able to enter the soil and leave trunks clear.
Plan spacing from mature plant size. Prepare nursery plants for the next suitable planting opportunity.

heading.text: Lulamisa Ndhawu yo Sungula leyi Hlayisekaka
heading.backTranslation: Prepare a Starting Place that can be Maintained

body.text: Sungula hi ndhawu leyi u nga yi cheletaka mati ni ku yi hlayisa. Kambela swimila leswi nga kona u nga si yi basisa.
body.backTranslation: Start with an area that you can water and look after. Check the plants that are already there before you clear it.

body.text: Laha swi faneleke, cardboard ya ntolovelo ehansi ka mulch lowu faneleke yi nga hunguta ku kula loku nga laviwiki. Pfumelela leswaku mati ma nghena emisaveni u siya minsinya ya mirhi (trunks) yi ri ni ndhawu yo basa.
body.backTranslation: Where suitable, ordinary cardboard under suitable mulch can reduce unwanted growth. Let water enter the soil, leaving the tree trunks with a clean space.

body.text: Hlela ndhawu leyi nga exikarhi ka swimila hi ku ya hi vukulu bya swona loko swi kurile. Lunghiselela nursery plants eka nkarhi wo byala lowu landzelaka lowu faneleke.
body.backTranslation: Plan the space in the middle of the plants according to their size when grown. Prepare nursery plants for the next suitable planting time.

english.heading: Adjust as the Trees Grow
body: Watch how shade, roots and available water affect neighbouring plants.
Comfrey and wild garlic appear in the original underplanting example; check their local suitability before use.
Prune or thin support plants when needed, using methods suited to each species. Suitable clean cuttings can return as mulch. Do not wait for a fixed year if competition is already harming plants.

heading.text: Lulamisa Loko Mirhi Yi Kula
heading.backTranslation: Adjust When Trees Grow

body.text: Languta ndlela leyi ndzhuti (shade), timitsu ni mati lama kumekaka swi khumbaka ha yona swimila leswi nga ekusuhi.
body.backTranslation: Look at the way that shade, roots and available water affect the plants that are nearby.

body.text: Comfrey ni wild garlic swi kumeka eka xikombiso xa masungulo xa ku byala ehansi ka mirhi; kambela ku fanela ka swona ka ndhawu u nga si swi tirhisa.
body.backTranslation: Comfrey and wild garlic are in the starting example of planting beneath trees; check their suitability for the site before using them.

body.text: Tsema marhavi ya support plants kumbe u endla thinning (ku susa support plants leswi hlawuriweke hi ku helela) loko swi laveka, u tirhisa tindlela leti fanelaka muxaka wun'wana ni wun'wana. Swilo leswi tsemiweke leswi faneleke leswi basileke swi nga vuyisiwa tanihi mulch. U nga rindzi lembe leri vekiweke loko ku phikizana se ku onha swimila.
body.backTranslation: Cut the branches of support plants or do thinning (removing selected support plants completely) when needed, using methods suited to each kind. Suitable clean cut material can be returned as mulch. Do not wait for a set year if competition is already damaging the plants.

english.heading: Plant with Reliable Moisture
body: Choose a planting opportunity when soil moisture and expected weather support establishment.
Rain can help, but check the root zone and keep a backup watering plan. Avoid planting into waterlogged ground.
Check young plants after planting. Harvest timing and outside inputs depend on the species, site and care; there is no guaranteed fifth-year result.

heading.text: Byala hi Mati lama Tshembekaka
heading.backTranslation: Plant with Reliable Water

body.text: Hlawula nkarhi wo byala loko ku tsakama ka misava ni xiyimo xa moya lexi languteriweke swi seketela establishment.
body.backTranslation: Choose the time to plant when soil moisture and the expected weather conditions support establishment.

body.text: Mpfula yi nga pfuna, kambe kambela root zone u tlhela u va ni pulani yo hlayisela ya ku cheleta mati. Papalata ku byala emisaveni leyi tatiweke hi mati.
body.backTranslation: Rain can help, but check the root zone and also have a backup plan for watering. Avoid planting in soil filled with water.

body.text: Kambela swimila leswintshwa endzhaku ka ku byala. Nkarhi wa ntshovelo (harvest) ni swilo leswi tisiwaka ku suka handle swi titshege hi muxaka, ndhawu ni nhlayiso; a ku na vuyelo lebyi tiyisekisiweke eka lembe ra vuntlhanu.
body.backTranslation: Check the new plants after planting. The harvest time and things brought in from outside depend on the kind, the site and care; there is no confirmed yield for the fifth year.

english.heading: Field Assignment
body: Draw the layers for your own proposed planting. Mark access, water and existing natural vegetation.
Record local frost, rain, soil and available care.
For each plant from the approved list, record its intended role and the local advice still needed before planting.

heading.text: Ntirho lowu u nyikiweke wa le nsimini
heading.backTranslation: The task given of the field

body.text: Dirowa swiyenge swa ku byala loku u ku kunguhateke. Komba ndlela yo fikelela, mati ni swimila swa ntumbuluko leswi nga kona.
body.backTranslation: Draw the planting areas/layers that you have planned. Show access, water and the natural plants that are present.

body.text: Tsala xiqhwa, mpfula, misava ni nhlayiso lowu kumekaka eka ndhawu ya wena.
body.backTranslation: Write down the frost, rain, soil and available care at your site.

body.text: Eka swimila swin'wana ni swin'wana leswi nga eka lisiti leyi pfumeriweke, tsala ntirho lowu swi kunguhatiweke ku wu endla ni ndzayo ya ndhawu leyi ha lavekaka u nga si byala.
body.backTranslation: For each plant on the approved list, write the job it is planned to do and the site advice that is still needed before planting.

english.heading: Field Action
body: Inspect a manageable area and choose one next step.
Protect exposed soil, check plant suitability, or prepare nursery plants.
Plant only when conditions and follow-up care are suitable. Return to the same spot to check survival, soil moisture and competition.

heading.text: Xiendlo xa le nsimini
heading.backTranslation: Field activity

body.text: Languta ndhawu leyi u nga kotaka ku yi hlayisa, kutani u hlawula goza rin’we leri landzelaka.
body.backTranslation: Look at the place that you can maintain, then choose one next step.

body.text: Sirhelela misava leyi nga funengetiwangiki, kambela ku fanela ka swimila kumbe u lulamisa nursery plants.
body.backTranslation: Protect uncovered soil; check the suitability of plants or prepare nursery plants.

body.text: Byala ntsena loko swiyimo ni nhlayiso lowu landzelaka swi fanerile. Tlhelela endhawini yin'we ku ya kambela ku hanya, ku tsakama ka misava ni ku phikizana.
body.backTranslation: Plant only when the conditions and the following care are suitable. Return to the same place to check survival, soil moisture and competition.
